First off, picture in your mind the same thing with no wheels at all. Just mentally erase the wheels. Chip runs exactly the same distance as Dale. (Is that Chip and Dale? Oh, well. I'm assuming for this discussion.)

Now think of the wheel and specifically the exact place that the wheel touches the ground. The wheel isn't slipping on the ground. Where the wheel touches the ground, that part of the wheel is stationary with respect to the ground. So the bottom of the wheel is moving under foot at exactly the same speed as the ground is moving under foot.

If both Chip and Dale are travelling over the ground at the same speed, and the bottom of the wheel is stationary with respect to the ground at the point that it touches, then they are running at the same speed inside their respective wheels. Even though the wheels themselves are different size.

Dale's wheel will rotate about 3 to 4 times for each rotation of Chip's wheel, but they are both running at the same speed and covering the same distance.
